title: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)
hook: the first person to speak in the Gita is not Krishna or Arjuna. it's Duryodhana, talking to his old teacher.
tomorrow: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)

segments.voice: Yesterday the Bhishma Parva opened in a dark room: a blind king refusing sight, and Sanjaya, a listener who chose to hear rather than see, telling him everything. What did you notice you'd rather hear about than see? Day eight hundred twenty.
screen: `THE KING CHOSE TO HEAR.` · `SANJAYA TELLS IT ALL.`

segments.voice: Ask someone how the Bhagavad Gita begins, and they may tell you about Arjuna's doubt, or Krishna's teaching. But after the old king's question, the first real speech belongs to someone else. Duryodhana walks over to Drona, the teacher who trained the princes on both sides, and starts talking. He names the great fighters on the other side. Then he names his own. It sounds like a general's briefing. Listen closer, and it sounds like a man reassuring himself. Today, session two of six: the noise before the silence.
screen: `WHO SPEAKS FIRST?` → `DURYODHANA, TO HIS TEACHER` → `THE NOISE BEFORE THE SILENCE`

segments.voice: Put yourself in the scene. Duryodhana stands before Drona and points across the field. Look at the Pandava army, he says, arrayed by your own student, Drupada's son. He's reminding his teacher, a little sharply, that the enemy commander learned from him too. Then he lists his own champions, with Bhishma at their head, and tells everyone to guard Bhishma. Bhishma doesn't answer in words. To cheer Duryodhana, the old grandsire roars like a lion and blows his conch shell. Then the field erupts. Conches, drums, horns, from the Kaurava side. And from the other side, Krishna blows his conch, Panchajanya. Arjuna blows his, Devadatta. Bhima blows a huge one, and the rest of the Pandava fighters join in. The Gita says that sound tore at the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons and made the earth and sky resound. Now hold that noise in your ears, because of what comes next. Arjuna lifts his bow and asks Krishna to drive the chariot out between the two armies, so he can see who he's about to fight. Krishna sets it down right in front of Bhishma and Drona. And Arjuna looks. Grandfathers. Teachers. Uncles. Brothers. Sons. Friends. His limbs give way. His bow, Gandiva, slips from his hand. He sits down in the chariot and sets his weapons aside. After all that sound, the first chapter ends with a man sitting still. That stillness is where Krishna's teaching begins.
screen: `DURYODHANA BRIEFS DRONA` · `BHISHMA'S CONCH, THEN EVERY CONCH` · `THE CHARIOT BETWEEN THE ARMIES` · then, large: `ARJUNA SITS DOWN`

segments.voice: Sit as you are. Whatever is busy around you or in your head, you don't need to quiet it. Start from the ground instead. Breathing out, let your feet go still. Next breath, your knees. Then your hands, your shoulders, your jaw. You aren't silencing the world. You're letting yourself sit down in the middle of it, the way Arjuna did between the armies. If you pray, you can begin your prayer from that stillness. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma Parva. The book named for the grandsire, whose conch started the noise that ends in Arjuna's silence.
Your line: a man sitting still. Today, once, in the loudest part of your day, stop and sit still for three breaths. Day eight hundred twenty.

howItsDone: The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is recited along with the rest, and the conches named in it, such as Krishna's Panchajanya, are familiar from pictures of Krishna and Arjuna in the chariot.

match.prompt: whose conch, whose words? tap the pairs.

myth: the first speech in the Gita, after the king's question, is Krishna's
it's Duryodhana's, spoken to his teacher Drona.
Bhishma blew his conch to cheer Duryodhana
he roared like a lion and blew it, and the conches of both armies followed.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. the conches have sounded. you ask Krishna to drive you between the armies, and you see your grandfather and teachers. what do you do?
options: drop your bow and sit down in the chariot.
turn the chariot and leave the field.
fork.reveal: his bow slips from his hand, and he sits down in the chariot. the first chapter of the Gita ends in that stillness.

original.note: shankha, the conch shell blown in battle in the Gita's first chapter, and still blown in Hindu worship.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Gita begins with Arjuna's doubt.
what it means: it begins with Duryodhana's briefing and a wall of noise, and only then Arjuna sits down.
what a scholar hears: the first chapter moves from the Kaurava side to the Pandava side, from sound to silence, before Krishna teaches.
recall: bites Nala and changes his shape
waits for a lapse, then enters Nala

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 1.2–1.19 (Bhishma Parva), Duryodhana speaks to Drona; the conches
Bhagavad Gita 1.20–1.47, Arjuna's chariot between the armies; he sets down his bow

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm: Duryodhana addresses Drona and names 'Drupada's son' (Dhrishtadyumna) as the arranger of the Pandava army, 'your intelligent disciple'; lists his champions; asks all to protect Bhishma; Bhishma roars and blows his conch to cheer him; Panchajanya (Krishna), Devadatta (Arjuna), Paundra (Bhima, not named in the script); the sound 'rent the hearts' of Dhritarashtra's sons and filled earth and sky.
'Sets it down right in front of Bhishma and Drona' follows 1.25.
Original note says the conch is 'still blown in Hindu worship'; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with that general statement.
Year 1 already read 1.20–1.27 verse by verse; this day's angle is the order of speakers and the move from noise to stillness.
Editor pass: review question matched to day 819's revised carry; 'trained both armies' narrowed to 'trained the princes on both sides'.

Audit (fresh pass): practice repeated day 819's sound-listening practice; rewritten as a feet-to-jaw stillness. 'Bhishma answers the only way the moment allows' overstated the text (1.12 gives no reply, only the roar and conch); now 'doesn't answer in words'. Pronunciation of shankha corrected to SHUNG-khuh.
